The operation may implement refresh token rotation as a security enhancement, where using a refresh token invalidates it and issues both a new access token and a new refresh token. When a user deletes their account, the system removes all associated data including the user account record, all todo items owned by that user, and all session records. This operation is associated with the todo_list_users table in the Prisma schema.

The deletion is permanent and irreversible - once an account is deleted, the user cannot recover their data. All todo items created by the user are also permanently removed from the system due to the cascade delete relationship defined in the schema. The user's email address becomes available for re-registration after account deletion.

This operation requires authentication to ensure only the account owner can delete their own account. The system validates that the requesting user is deleting their own account and not attempting to delete another user's account. After successful deletion, all session tokens for that user are invalidated, and the user must create a new account if they wish to use the service again.
operations.description:
Permanently delete the authenticated user's account and all associated data from the Todo list application. This operation provides users with complete control over their data and enables them to remove their presence from the system entirely.

When a user deletes their account, the system performs a cascade deletion that removes all data associated with that user account. This includes the user account record itself from the todo_list_users table, all todo items owned by the user from the todo_list_todos table (due to the onDelete: Cascade relationship), and all session records from the todo_list_user_sessions table. The deletion is atomic - either all associated data is removed successfully, or the operation fails and no data is deleted.

This operation implements hard delete functionality. The Prisma schema includes a deleted_at field in the todo_list_users table for soft delete capability, but this operation performs permanent deletion by completely removing the user record from the database. This ensures that the user's email address becomes immediately available for re-registration and that no personal data remains in the system.

Security considerations are paramount for this operation. The system verifies that the authenticated user is deleting their own account by extracting the user ID from the JWT token and ensuring it matches the account being deleted. Users cannot delete other users' accounts. After successful deletion, all active session tokens for that user are invalidated, preventing any further access using old tokens.

This operation aligns with data privacy best practices and user data control requirements. Users have the right to remove their data from the system, and this operation fulfills that requirement. The frontend application should implement a confirmation dialog to prevent accidental account deletions, but the backend executes the deletion immediately upon receiving a valid authenticated request.

Error scenarios include authentication failures (user not logged in), authorization failures (though users can only delete their own accounts), and database errors during the deletion process. The system provides clear error messages for each scenario while maintaining security by not exposing internal system details.

This operation allows an authenticated user to change their password securely. The password change process requires the user to provide their current password for verification before setting a new password. This operation is associated with the todo_list_users table in the Prisma schema, specifically updating the password_hash field.

Password changes must meet the same security requirements as initial registration: minimum 8 characters, at least one letter, and at least one number. The system validates the new password against these requirements before proceeding. The current password is verified by comparing the provided value against the stored password_hash using secure password comparison methods.

When a password is successfully changed, the system updates the password_hash field with the new hashed password and updates the updated_at timestamp in the todo_list_users table. For security reasons, all existing refresh tokens for the user should be invalidated (except potentially the current session), forcing re-authentication on other devices. This prevents unauthorized access if the password change was initiated due to suspected account compromise.
operations.description:
Change the password for the authenticated user's account. This operation enables users to update their password for security purposes, such as maintaining password hygiene, responding to suspected account compromise, or updating to a stronger password.

The password change process requires two pieces of information from the user: their current password and the new password they wish to set. The current password requirement serves as an additional security verification to ensure that an attacker who has obtained access to an authenticated session cannot change the password without knowing the original password. This prevents session hijacking attacks from completely taking over an account.

The system validates the current password by comparing it against the password_hash stored in the todo_list_users table. This comparison must use secure password verification methods that prevent timing attacks. If the current password does not match, the operation fails immediately with an authentication error, and the system may log this failed attempt for security monitoring purposes.

The new password must meet all password strength requirements defined in the business rules: minimum 8 characters in length, containing at least one letter, and containing at least one number. The system validates the new password against these requirements before accepting it. If the new password fails validation, the operation returns a detailed error message specifying which requirements were not met, helping users create a compliant password.

When the password change is successful, the system performs several security operations. First, it hashes the new password using the same industry-standard algorithm used during registration (bcrypt, argon2, or PBKDF2) and updates the password_hash field in the todo_list_users table. Second, it updates the updated_at timestamp to reflect the modification. Third, it should invalidate all existing refresh tokens associated with the user account except potentially the current session, which forces the user to log in again on all other devices.

This token invalidation is a critical security measure. If a user changes their password because they suspect their account has been compromised, invalidating all sessions ensures that any attacker who gained access is immediately logged out. The user remains logged in on the device where they changed the password, providing a seamless experience while maintaining security.

The operation requires authentication - users must be logged in to change their password. The system extracts the user ID from the JWT token to identify which user account's password should be changed. Users can only change their own password; there is no ability to change another user's password through this endpoint.

After a successful password change, the system should send a confirmation email to the user's registered email address notifying them of the password change. This provides an additional security notification in case the password was changed by an unauthorized party who gained access to an authenticated session.

operations.description:
This endpoint handles administrator authentication, allowing admins to log into the system with their credentials and gain access to administrative functions. This is a critical security operation that validates admin identity and establishes an authenticated session with elevated privileges.

The authentication process follows industry-standard security practices: the admin provides their email address and password through the request body. The system validates the email exists in the todo_list_admins table, then verifies the provided password against the stored password_hash using secure comparison methods (constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks). The password is never transmitted or stored in plain text, and the system uses industry-standard hashing algorithms like bcrypt, argon2, or PBKDF2.

Upon successful authentication, the system performs several operations: generates JWT access and refresh tokens containing the admin's ID and role, creates a new session record in the todo_list_admin_sessions table with metadata including IP address, connection URL, and referrer for audit purposes, and returns the tokens along with admin profile information to the client. The access token typically expires after 15-30 minutes, while the refresh token has a longer lifespan of 7-30 days.

Security measures include protection against brute force attacks through rate limiting and temporary delays after multiple failed attempts, generic error messages that don't reveal whether the email or password was incorrect to prevent account enumeration, and comprehensive logging of all authentication attempts for security monitoring and audit trails.

If authentication fails due to invalid credentials, non-existent email, or disabled admin account, the system returns an appropriate error without exposing sensitive information about which credential was incorrect. This endpoint is publicly accessible (no authentication required to attempt login) but implements strict security controls to protect against unauthorized access.

operations.description:
This operation provides a comprehensive session termination mechanism that logs out the currently authenticated administrator from every active session across all devices and browsers simultaneously. When an admin invokes this endpoint, the system validates their JWT access token to identify the admin, then locates all active session records in the todo_list_admin_sessions table where expired_at is null, and marks all of them as expired by setting the expired_at timestamp to the current time.

This global logout functionality serves critical security purposes. If an administrator suspects their account credentials have been compromised, lost a device, or used a public computer and forgot to log out, they can use this operation to immediately revoke access from all locations. After successful execution, all existing JWT access tokens for this admin become invalid, and the admin must re-authenticate on every device to regain access to the system.

The operation maintains complete audit trails by recording expiration timestamps for all affected sessions. This provides administrators and security teams with visibility into when global logouts occurred, which can be correlated with security incidents or policy compliance requirements. The system logs this significant security event with appropriate detail for administrative oversight.

Unlike the standard logout operation which only terminates the current session, this endpoint affects every active session simultaneously. This makes it particularly valuable for security-conscious administrators who want to ensure no unauthorized access remains, for admins changing their passwords who want to force re-authentication everywhere, or for security teams responding to potential account compromise. When a todo item is successfully created, the system automatically performs several actions based on the todo_list_todos schema: assigns the todo to the authenticated user (sets todo_list_user_id from the JWT token), sets the completion status to 'incomplete', records the current timestamp in both created_at and updated_at fields, and sets deleted_at to null. The system generates a unique identifier for the new todo item and returns the complete todo object to the user.

Security and authorization: This operation requires valid authentication via JWT token. The system extracts the user ID from the token and uses it to establish ownership of the new todo item. Users can only create todos for themselves - there is no ability to create todos for other users. This ensures proper data isolation and privacy boundaries.

Validation rules enforced: Title must be provided and cannot be empty or contain only whitespace. Title length must be between 1 and 200 characters after trimming. Description, if provided, must not exceed 2,000 characters. If validation fails, the operation returns detailed error messages indicating which requirements were not met.

The newly created todo item becomes immediately available in the user's todo list and can be viewed, updated, marked complete, or deleted through other API operations. The creation timestamp enables chronological sorting and organization of tasks.

Security considerations include strict user isolation - each authenticated user can only access their own todo items. The system automatically filters results to include only todos where todo_list_user_id matches the authenticated user. The response excludes soft-deleted todos (where deleted_at is not null) to maintain data consistency.

This operation integrates with the todo_list_todos table as defined in the Prisma schema, utilizing indexes on todo_list_user_id, status, and created_at for optimal query performance. The GIN index on title enables efficient text search capabilities. The response includes todo summary information optimized for list displays, with options to filter by status and search within title text.

Retrieve complete details of a single todo item identified by its unique ID. This operation returns all information associated with the todo including the title, optional description, completion status, creation timestamp, and last modification timestamp.

Before returning the todo item, the system verifies that the todo_list_user_id of the requested todo matches the authenticated user's ID. If the todo belongs to a different user, the system denies access with a 403 Forbidden error, preventing unauthorized access to other users' personal task data.

The system excludes soft-deleted todos from retrieval - if the requested todo has a non-null deleted_at timestamp, it is treated as not found. This maintains consistency with the soft delete pattern while allowing for potential future recovery features.

The response provides the complete todo entity with all fields populated, enabling detailed viewing and editing workflows. Users typically access this endpoint when they want to view full details of a todo item, edit its properties, or review task information before marking it complete.

The system validates that the provided todoId exists and belongs to the authenticated user before allowing any modifications. If a user attempts to update another user's todo item, the request is denied with an authorization error.

All updated data undergoes the same validation as creation: the title must be non-empty and within length limits (1-200 characters), the description must not exceed maximum length (2000 characters), and the status must be either 'complete' or 'incomplete'. The system automatically updates the updated_at timestamp to the current time while preserving the original created_at timestamp and user ownership. The deleted_at field remains unchanged during updates.

This operation supports partial updates, allowing users to modify individual fields without requiring all fields to be provided. Users can update just the title, just the description, just the status, or any combination of these fields. The unchanged fields retain their existing values.

operations.summary: Soft delete a todo item by setting its deleted_at timestamp
operations.description:
Performs soft deletion of a todo item from the todo_list_todos table by setting the deleted_at timestamp to the current date and time. This operation enables users to remove todos they no longer need while preserving the data for potential recovery or audit purposes. The todo item remains in the database but is marked as deleted and will no longer appear in the user's active todo list.

The operation enforces strict ownership verification - users can only delete their own todo items. The system validates that the provided todoId exists and belongs to the authenticated user before allowing deletion. If a user attempts to delete another user's todo item, the request is denied with an authorization error. If the todo item does not exist or has already been deleted, the system returns an appropriate not found error.

Once a todo is soft deleted, it is immediately removed from all todo list views and queries for active items. The deleted_at timestamp is set to the current time, while all other fields (title, description, status, created_at, updated_at) remain unchanged. This soft delete approach maintains the complete history of the todo item while making it inaccessible to normal operations.

Soft deletion provides several benefits over hard deletion: it enables potential future recovery features where users could restore accidentally deleted todos, maintains referential integrity in the database, supports audit trails and compliance requirements, and preserves historical data for analytics purposes.

If a user attempts to mark another user's todo item as complete, the system denies access with an authorization error.

This operation is idempotent - if a todo item is already marked as complete, the operation succeeds without error and updates the updated_at timestamp. The completion status change is immediately visible to the user, and the todo item will appear in filtered views showing completed tasks. This operation is fundamental to the todo list workflow, enabling users to experience the satisfaction of completing tasks and maintaining an organized view of finished versus pending work.

href.description:

The value can be an empty string for direct access (when users navigate directly to the registration page rather than being referred from another page). The server cannot infer this client-side navigation context, so it must be provided by the client application.

ITodoListUser.IRegister.description:
Registration request containing user credentials and session context for new account creation.

This schema defines the data required when a new user registers for the Todo list application. It includes the core authentication credentials (email and password) that establish the user's identity, along with session context fields (ip, href, referrer) that capture the registration environment for security auditing and user experience tracking.

The email and password fields are mandatory as they form the foundation of the user's account and authentication mechanism. The password undergoes security validation to ensure it meets minimum strength requirements before account creation proceeds.

The session context fields (href and referrer) are required because registration is a self-signup operation where the user is creating their own account and will be immediately authenticated. The ip field is optional as the server can extract it from the request, though clients may provide it explicitly for server-side rendering scenarios.

Upon successful validation of this registration data, the system creates a new record in the todo_list_users table with a unique UUID identifier, stores the email, hashes the password for secure storage, sets created_at and updated_at timestamps, and leaves deleted_at as null for the active account. Simultaneously, the system creates a session record in todo_list_user_sessions to track the initial login session established during registration.

The registration process provides an optimal user experience by combining account creation and authentication in a single operation, allowing users to immediately access the application without requiring a separate login step after registration.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated user.

This is the primary key (todo_list_users.id) that uniquely identifies the user account in the system. It is included in JWT token payloads and used throughout the application to associate todo items and other resources with the user.

This UUID remains constant for the lifetime of the user account and is used in authorization checks to ensure users can only access their own data.

email.description:
User's email address from the authenticated account.

This is the email field from todo_list_users table that serves as the user's unique identifier and login credential. It is included in the response to provide the client with the authenticated user's profile information.

The email is also included in the JWT access token payload for user identification in subsequent requests.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the user account was created.

This is the created_at field from the todo_list_users table, indicating when the user originally registered for the Todo list application. It provides account age information and is useful for user profile displays.

The timestamp is in ISO 8601 format and represents the exact moment the user account was first established in the system.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the user account was last modified.

This field is automatically updated by the system whenever any profile information changes, such as email updates. It maintains an audit trail of the most recent account modification.

Stored as a timezone-aware timestamp in the updated_at column of todo_list_users.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the user account was soft deleted.

This is the deleted_at field from the todo_list_users table. When null, the account is active and operational. When a timestamp is present, it indicates the account has been soft deleted, allowing for potential recovery and maintaining audit trails.

Soft deleted accounts cannot authenticate or access the system, but the account data is preserved for historical and compliance purposes. This enables account recovery if needed and maintains referential integrity with related data.

Stored as a nullable timezone-aware timestamp in the deleted_at column of todo_list_users.

ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.description:
Authenticated user profile with JWT tokens.

This response represents a successfully authenticated user, containing their profile information along with the JWT access and refresh tokens needed for subsequent authenticated API requests. It is returned after successful login or token refresh operations.

The response includes the user's unique identifier, email address, account creation timestamp, last modification timestamp, and soft deletion status from the todo_list_users table, along with both authentication tokens. The access token enables immediate API request authentication with 15-minute validity, while the refresh token allows obtaining new access tokens for 30 days without re-authentication.

The deleted_at field provides visibility into the account's soft delete status, which is important for understanding account state even though soft deleted accounts cannot authenticate. This field will be null for all successful authentication responses since deleted accounts cannot log in.

This structure establishes the authenticated session that authorizes the user to perform all todo management operations on their personal todo items, enforcing data isolation where users can only access todo_list_todos records with todo_list_user_id matching their authenticated user ID.

email.description:
User's email address for authentication.

This must match the email stored in the todo_list_users table. The system validates that the email format is correct and checks if an account exists with this email address. The email serves as the username for login and must be unique across all users.

For security reasons, authentication failure messages do not specify whether the email or password was incorrect, preventing account enumeration attacks.

password.description:
User's password for authentication verification.

This is the plain text password provided by the user for login. The system compares this against the password_hash stored in the todo_list_users table using secure comparison methods (constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks).

The password is transmitted securely over HTTPS and is never stored in plain text. After validation, it is immediately discarded. The system uses industry-standard hashing algorithms (bcrypt, argon2, or PBKDF2) to verify the password matches the stored hash.

Minimum password requirements (enforced during registration) include at least 8 characters length, at least one letter, and at least one number.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring.

This is the IP address from which the user is connecting to establish the session. The IP is recorded in the todo_list_user_sessions table for security auditing, unusual activity detection, and session management purposes.

While the server can typically extract the IP address from the request headers, the client may provide it explicitly for scenarios like server-side rendering (SSR) where the actual client IP needs to be passed through. If not provided, the server will extract it from the request.

This field is optional - if omitted or null, the server will determine the IP address from the HTTP request.

href.description:
Connection URL where the login session is being initiated.

This is the current page URL from which the user is logging in. It is recorded in the todo_list_user_sessions table as part of the session metadata for tracking user login contexts and navigation patterns.

The href provides valuable context about where users are logging in from, which pages are entry points for authentication, and helps in debugging authentication issues. It must be a valid URI format.

This field is required and must be provided by the client application.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that led to the login page.

This is the previous page URL that the user was on before navigating to the login page. It is recorded in the todo_list_user_sessions table as part of the session metadata for understanding user navigation flows and login contexts.

The referrer helps track how users are arriving at the login page, whether from external sites, internal navigation, or direct access. For direct access to the login page, this may be an empty string. It must be a valid URI format when provided.

This field is required and must be provided by the client application.

ITodoListUser.ILogin.description:
User login credentials with session context information.

This type represents the information required for a user to authenticate and establish a session in the Todo list application. It includes the user's email and password for credential verification, along with session context fields (ip, href, referrer) that are recorded in the todo_list_user_sessions table.

The session context fields are important for security monitoring, audit trails, and understanding user login patterns. The href and referrer fields are mandatory as the server cannot infer them, while the ip field is optional since the server can extract it from the request (though the client may provide it for SSR scenarios).

Upon successful authentication, the system validates the credentials against the todo_list_users table, creates a new session record in todo_list_user_sessions with the provided context information, generates JWT access and refresh tokens, and returns the authorization information to establish an authenticated session.

refresh_token.description:
Valid JWT refresh token to exchange for a new access token.

This is the long-lived refresh token (30-day expiration) that was previously issued during login or a prior token refresh operation. The system will validate this token to ensure it is properly signed, not expired, not revoked, and belongs to an active user account.

The refresh token enables users to obtain new access tokens when their current access token expires after 15 minutes, allowing seamless session continuation without requiring email and password re-authentication. The token contains the user's identity information and is validated against the system's revoked token list to prevent reuse of invalidated tokens.

Refresh tokens are revoked on logout, password change, or 'logout from all devices' operations to maintain security.

ITodoListUser.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token request for obtaining a new access token.

This request body contains the valid refresh token needed to generate a new access token when the current access token expires. The refresh token mechanism enables continuous user sessions without frequent re-authentication while maintaining security through short-lived access tokens.

The system validates that the provided refresh token is properly signed with the JWT secret key, has not exceeded its 30-day expiration period, has not been revoked (tokens are revoked on logout or password change), and belongs to an active user in the todo_list_users table (where deleted_at is null).

Upon successful validation, the system generates a new JWT access token with 15-minute expiration and may implement refresh token rotation by also issuing a new refresh token. This operation is essential for maintaining authenticated sessions in the Todo list application while keeping access tokens short-lived for security purposes.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated user.

This is the primary key from the todo_list_users table, automatically assigned by the system during registration. The ID uniquely identifies the user across the application and is used for session management and data ownership verification.

token.description:
JWT token information for authentication and session management.

Contains both access and refresh tokens required for maintaining authenticated sessions. The access token is used for immediate API request authentication, while the refresh token enables obtaining new access tokens when they expire.

ITodoListUser.IAuthorization.description:
Authorization response containing authenticated user information and access tokens.

This type represents the successful authentication result returned after a user logs in with valid credentials. It provides all necessary information for the client application to establish and maintain an authenticated session, including the user's identity, email address, and JWT tokens for API access.

The response enables the client to store the access token for subsequent API requests, use the refresh token to obtain new access tokens when they expire, identify the authenticated user in the application UI, and maintain session state across the application.

This authorization information is returned from login operations and token refresh operations, establishing the foundation for all authenticated interactions with the Todo list application.

created_at.description:

This field is automatically set by the system during admin account creation and represents the exact date and time when the admin user was registered in the system. This timestamp is immutable and provides an audit trail of when the account was established. It can be used for account age calculations and historical tracking.

updated_at.description:

This field is automatically updated by the system whenever any profile information changes, such as email updates or password modifications. It provides a record of the most recent account modification and helps track account activity. The system maintains this timestamp to support audit trails and change tracking.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the administrator account was soft deleted.

When this field is null, the account is active and operational. When a timestamp is present, it indicates the account has been soft deleted, allowing for potential recovery and maintaining audit trails. Soft deleted accounts typically cannot authenticate or perform admin operations, but the account data is preserved for historical and compliance purposes.

ITodoListAdmin.description:
Administrator account profile information.

Represents the complete profile data for a system administrator user, including their unique identifier, authentication email, and account lifecycle timestamps. This type is returned when retrieving admin profile information and contains all non-sensitive account details. The password hash is intentionally excluded from this response type for security purposes, ensuring that authentication credentials are never exposed through API responses.

Administrators have elevated privileges for system management and user support. They can view system-wide statistics, manage user accounts, and access administrative dashboard functionality. However, even admins respect user privacy and should only access individual user data when necessary for legitimate support or administrative purposes.

The account includes soft delete capability through the deleted_at timestamp, which enables account recovery and maintains audit trails even after account deletion. Active accounts have a null deleted_at value, while soft deleted accounts contain the deletion timestamp.

href.description:
Connection URL where the registration is occurring.

Mandatory field representing the current page URL where the admin is registering. This is stored in the todo_list_admin_sessions table as part of the session context and helps track registration sources, supports analytics, and aids in security monitoring by recording where admin accounts are being created.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that led to the registration page.

Mandatory field capturing the previous page URL before the admin navigated to the registration page. Can be an empty string for direct access. This is stored in the todo_list_admin_sessions table and helps understand registration sources, supports marketing attribution, and aids in security analysis by tracking how admins discovered the registration page.

email.description:
Administrator's email address used for authentication.

This email address must match an email in the todo_list_admins table. The system uses this to identify the admin account attempting to log in. The email is validated for proper email format and checked against the database to verify it exists.

For security reasons, if the email does not exist in the system, the error message will not explicitly reveal this fact to prevent account enumeration attacks. Instead, a generic authentication failure message is returned.

password.description:
Administrator's password in plain text for verification.

This password will be validated against the password_hash stored in the todo_list_admins table. The password is transmitted in plain text (over HTTPS in production) but is immediately hashed and compared using secure methods that prevent timing attacks. The plain text password is never stored or logged.

The system uses industry-standard hashing algorithms like bcrypt, argon2, or PBKDF2 to securely verify the password. If the password does not match, the authentication fails with a generic error message that does not reveal whether the email or password was incorrect.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security auditing.

This field is optional as the server can typically extract the IP address from the HTTP request headers. However, in certain scenarios (such as server-side rendering or proxy configurations), the client may need to provide the actual end-user IP address explicitly.

The IP address is stored in the todo_list_admin_sessions table and used for security monitoring, detecting suspicious login patterns, and maintaining audit trails of administrative access.

href.description:
Connection URL where the admin session was initiated.

This represents the current page URL from which the admin is logging in. It is stored in the todo_list_admin_sessions table for audit purposes and helps track the context of admin logins.

This field is mandatory as the server cannot infer this information from the request alone. It must be provided by the client application.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that led to the admin login page.

This represents the previous page URL that directed the admin to the login page. It is stored in the todo_list_admin_sessions table for audit purposes and helps understand how admins are accessing the system.

This field is mandatory as the server cannot reliably infer this information. If the admin accessed the login page directly (no referrer), this can be an empty string.

ITodoListAdmin.ILogin.description:
Admin login credentials and session context for authentication.

This schema represents all data required for administrator authentication. It includes the admin's email and password for credential verification, as well as session context fields (ip, href, referrer) that are stored in the todo_list_admin_sessions table for security auditing and tracking.

The email and password fields are used to authenticate the admin against the todo_list_admins table. The session context fields (href and referrer are mandatory, ip is optional) are metadata about the connection that help maintain audit trails and detect suspicious activity patterns.

When an admin logs in, this information is validated, and upon success, a new record is created in the todo_list_admin_sessions table containing the admin's ID and all the session context metadata.

refreshToken.description:
Valid JWT refresh token for obtaining a new access token.

This is the refresh token that was previously issued during login or a previous refresh operation. The refresh token has a longer lifespan (typically 30 days) compared to access tokens (15 minutes) and enables admins to obtain new access tokens without re-entering their credentials.

The system validates this token by verifying its signature using the secret key, checking its expiration timestamp, extracting the admin id from the payload, and confirming the associated admin account exists in todo_list_admins and is active (deleted_at is null).

The system also checks that the refresh token has not been revoked by validating the tokenId from the token payload against any revocation list. Refresh tokens are revoked when an admin logs out, changes their password, or requests logout from all devices.

Security: The refresh token must be stored securely by the client (preferably in httpOnly cookies or secure storage) and transmitted only over HTTPS. If a refresh token is compromised, it can be used to obtain access tokens until it expires or is explicitly revoked.

ITodoListAdmin.IRefresh.description:
Admin token refresh request containing the refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This interface defines the data required for an administrator to refresh their authentication session by exchanging a valid refresh token for a new access token. This enables continuous access to administrative functions without requiring credential re-entry when access tokens expire.

The refresh process validates the provided refresh token's signature, expiration, and revocation status, then verifies the associated admin account is still active in the todo_list_admins table. Upon successful validation, a new access token is generated.

Optionally, the system may implement refresh token rotation where using a refresh token generates both a new access token and a new refresh token, with the old refresh token being invalidated. This security measure limits the lifespan of any individual refresh token.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated administrator.

This is the primary key from the todo_list_admins table representing the admin who successfully authenticated. The ID uniquely identifies this admin across the system and is included in JWT token payloads for subsequent authenticated requests.

This identifier is used to associate all administrative actions with the specific admin who performed them, enabling audit trails and accountability for system management operations.

email.description:
Administrator's email address for authentication and system communications.

This email serves as the unique username for admin login and is used for all system communications with the administrator. It must follow valid email format and be unique across all admin accounts. The email can be updated through the profile update operation, but uniqueness is always enforced to prevent conflicts.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the administrator account was created.

This field is automatically set by the system during admin account creation and represents the exact date and time when the admin user was registered in the system. This timestamp is immutable and provides an audit trail of when the account was established. It can be used for account age calculations and historical tracking.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the administrator account was last modified.

This field is automatically updated by the system whenever any profile information changes, such as email updates or password modifications. It provides a record of the most recent account modification and helps track account activity. The system maintains this timestamp to support audit trails and change tracking.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the administrator account was soft deleted.

When this field is null, the account is active and operational. When a timestamp is present, it indicates the account has been soft deleted, allowing for potential recovery and maintaining audit trails. Soft deleted accounts typically cannot authenticate or perform admin operations, but the account data is preserved for historical and compliance purposes.

ITodoListAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Admin authorization response containing tokens and authenticated admin identity.

This interface defines the response returned after successful admin authentication (login, registration, or token refresh operations). It provides the admin's unique identifier and JWT tokens necessary for making authenticated requests to administrative endpoints.

The response includes complete admin profile information from the todo_list_admins table (id, email, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) along with a token object containing both access and refresh tokens. The access token is used for immediate authentication of subsequent requests with 15-30 minute expiration, while the refresh token enables obtaining new access tokens when the current one expires with 7-30 day expiration.

The deleted_at field is optional in the response because it may be null for active accounts. This field provides transparency about account status - when null, the account is fully active and operational. When a timestamp is present, it indicates soft deletion status for audit and recovery purposes.

Security: The tokens must be stored securely by the client and transmitted only over HTTPS. The access token should be included in the Authorization header of subsequent requests as 'Bearer {token}'. The refresh token should be stored separately and used only for token refresh operations to obtain new access tokens without credential re-entry.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated administrator.

This is the admin's primary key from the todo_list_admins table. It uniquely identifies the admin account across the entire system and is used in subsequent authenticated requests to identify which admin is making the request.

token.description:
JWT token information for admin authentication.

This object contains both the access token and refresh token that the admin client will use for subsequent authenticated requests. The access token is short-lived (typically 15-30 minutes) and must be included in the Authorization header of API requests. The refresh token is long-lived (typically 7-30 days) and is used to obtain new access tokens when the current one expires.

The tokens contain the admin's ID and role (admin) and are signed using the system's secret key to prevent tampering.

email.description:
Administrator's email address.

This is the email associated with the authenticated admin account from the todo_list_admins table. It is returned for display purposes and to confirm which account was authenticated.

session_id.description:
Unique identifier of the newly created admin session.

This is the primary key of the newly created record in the todo_list_admin_sessions table. It represents this specific login session and can be used to track or manage the session later (for example, for logout or session management operations).

ITodoListAdmin.ILoginResponse.description:
Response body returned upon successful admin authentication via login.

This schema represents all data returned to the admin client after successful login. It includes the admin's core profile information (id, email), authentication tokens for subsequent API requests, and the session identifier for tracking this specific login session.

The token object contains JWT access and refresh tokens that the client must store securely and use for authentication in subsequent requests. The session_id represents the record created in the todo_list_admin_sessions table and can be used for session management operations like logout.

This response provides everything the admin client needs to establish an authenticated session with elevated privileges and make authorized API requests to administrative endpoints. The session_id enables tracking and managing the admin's login session throughout its lifecycle.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the user account.

This is the primary key of the todo_list_users table, automatically generated by the system using UUID format. The ID is immutable and serves as the permanent reference for the user throughout the system.

This identifier is used to establish ownership of todo items and to link user sessions, ensuring data isolation and proper authorization boundaries.

email.description:
User's email address for authentication and account recovery.

The email must follow valid email format and is unique across all users in the system. This field is used for login authentication and for sending password reset emails and other account-related communications.

The email uniqueness constraint (@@unique([email])) in the todo_list_users table ensures no duplicate email addresses exist.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the user account was created.

This field is automatically set by the system during registration and cannot be modified. It provides an audit trail of when the account was established and is used for account age calculations and chronological sorting.

Stored as a timezone-aware timestamp in the created_at column of todo_list_users.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the user account was last modified.

This field is automatically updated by the system whenever any profile information changes, such as email updates. It maintains an audit trail of the most recent account modification.

Stored as a timezone-aware timestamp in the updated_at column of todo_list_users.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the user account was soft deleted.

When this field is null, the account is active and operational. When a timestamp is present, it indicates the account has been soft deleted, allowing for potential recovery and maintaining audit trails.

Soft deleted accounts cannot authenticate or access the system, but the account data is preserved in the todo_list_users table for historical and compliance purposes. This enables account recovery if needed and maintains referential integrity with related data.

Stored as a nullable timezone-aware timestamp in the deleted_at column of todo_list_users.

ITodoListUser.description:
Complete user account information returned in response to profile operations.

This DTO represents the full user profile data structure from the todo_list_users table, returned after successful profile updates, retrievals, or administrative operations. It includes all account details that reflect the complete state of the user entity in the database.

The response includes both active and soft-deleted account states through the deleted_at field. When deleted_at is null, the account is active and the user can authenticate and use the system. When deleted_at contains a timestamp, the account has been soft deleted and the user cannot access the system, though the data is preserved for audit trails and potential recovery.

Sensitive fields are intentionally excluded from this response type for security reasons. The password_hash field is never exposed in API responses as it contains hashed credentials that must remain protected.

This response type provides users and administrators with complete visibility into account details, including the unique identifier, registered email address, and temporal metadata showing when the account was created, last modified, and potentially soft deleted. This information helps verify account status, track account history, and support administrative oversight.

The structure follows REST best practices by returning the complete updated resource after modification operations, allowing clients to refresh their local state with the server's authoritative representation of the user account.

This DTO is used across multiple user management operations, including profile updates, profile retrieval, administrative user viewing, and soft delete operations where the complete account state including deletion timestamp needs to be communicated.

email.description:
Email address for the new user account.

Must follow valid email format conventions (contains @ symbol, valid domain structure) and must not already be registered in the system. The email serves as the username for authentication and is used for account recovery and system communications.

The system validates email uniqueness before account creation to prevent duplicate registrations.

password.description:
Plain text password for the new user account.

Must meet minimum security requirements: at least 8 characters in length, contain at least one letter, and contain at least one number. The system encourages but does not mandate special characters for enhanced security.

This password is transmitted in plain text only during the registration request, then immediately hashed using industry-standard algorithms (bcrypt, argon2, or PBKDF2) before storage. The plain text password is never stored or logged by the system.

The hashed password will be stored in the password_hash field of the todo_list_users table.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking (optional).

The IP address from which the registration request originates. This field is optional because the server can extract the IP address from the request headers. However, clients may provide it explicitly in server-side rendering scenarios or when operating through proxies.

Used for security monitoring, fraud detection, and creating the initial user session record in todo_list_user_sessions table.

href.description:
Connection URL where registration occurs (required).

The current page URL from which the user is registering. This is mandatory because the server cannot infer this information - only the client knows the exact page URL where the registration form was displayed.

Used for session tracking, analytics, and understanding user registration sources. Stored in the todo_list_user_sessions table as part of the initial session creation.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that led to registration (required).

The previous page URL that directed the user to the registration page. This is mandatory because the server cannot infer this information - only the client knows where the user came from.

Used for marketing attribution, understanding user acquisition channels, and tracking registration sources. Can be an empty string for direct access. Stored in the todo_list_user_sessions table as part of the initial session creation.

ITodoListUser.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new user account through registration.

This schema defines the data required when a new user registers for the Todo list application. It includes authentication credentials (email and password) and session context information (IP address, connection URL, and referrer) needed to establish the user's initial session.

The registration process validates email format and uniqueness, enforces password security requirements, securely hashes the password before storage, creates the user record in todo_list_users table, and establishes the initial session in todo_list_user_sessions table.

Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are included because registration is a self-signup operation where the user themselves creates their account and establishes their first session immediately. The ip field is optional (server can extract), while href and referrer are required (only client knows these values).

Security considerations: The password field accepts plain text only during transmission over HTTPS. The system immediately hashes the password using secure algorithms before any storage or logging. The email and password combination enables future authentication via login operations.

email.description:
New email address for the user account.

The email must follow valid email format conventions and must be unique across all users in the system. The system validates that the provided email is not already registered to another user account before accepting the update.

This field maps to the email column in the todo_list_users table, which has a unique constraint (@@unique([email])) enforcing email uniqueness at the database level.

When the email is successfully updated, the updated_at timestamp in todo_list_users is automatically set to the current time to maintain an audit trail of account modifications.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating the authenticated user's profile information.

This DTO allows users to modify their account details in the todo_list_users table. Currently, it supports updating the email address, which is the primary modifiable profile field in the minimal version of the application.

All fields are optional, following the partial update pattern. Users can choose to update only the fields they want to change without needing to provide all profile information. If no fields are provided, the operation effectively becomes a no-op but will still update the updated_at timestamp.

The operation automatically identifies which user account to update from the JWT authentication token, ensuring users can only modify their own profile. The user_id is never accepted in the request body as it comes from the authenticated session context.

System-managed fields are excluded from this DTO and cannot be modified through profile updates. These include: id (immutable primary key), password_hash (use dedicated password change endpoints), created_at (immutable creation timestamp), updated_at (automatically managed by the system), and deleted_at (managed through account deletion operations).

Validation rules enforce that if an email is provided, it must be in valid email format and must not already exist for another user account. The email uniqueness constraint prevents duplicate email addresses across the system.

Future enhancements may add additional optional fields such as display name, profile preferences, or notification settings, all following the same optional pattern to support partial updates.

email.description:
Email address of the user account requiring password reset.

This is the email address associated with the user account in the todo_list_users table. The system will use this email to identify the user and send password reset instructions.

For security reasons, the system does not reveal whether this email exists in the database. The response will be the same regardless of whether the email is found, preventing account enumeration attacks.

The email must be in valid email format containing @ symbol and valid domain structure.

ITodoListUser.IPasswordResetRequest.description:
Request body for initiating a password reset process.

This schema represents the data required when a user has forgotten their password and needs to reset it. The user provides their registered email address, and the system will send password reset instructions to that email if it exists in the system.

The operation implements security best practices by not revealing whether the provided email exists in the system, preventing attackers from using this functionality to enumerate valid user accounts.

This DTO is used for unauthenticated requests since users who have forgotten their passwords cannot log in.

message.description:
Generic success message that does not reveal whether the email exists in the system.

For security purposes, this message is intentionally vague and does not confirm whether the email address was found in the database. This prevents attackers from using the password reset functionality to enumerate valid user accounts.

Typical message: 'If an account exists with this email, you will receive password reset instructions.'

This approach ensures that the system response is identical whether the email exists or not, protecting user privacy and preventing information disclosure attacks.

ITodoListUser.IPasswordResetResponse.description:
Response body confirming that password reset instructions have been sent if the account exists.

This schema represents the system's response after processing a password reset request. For security reasons, the response does not reveal whether the provided email address exists in the system. This prevents account enumeration attacks where attackers could use the password reset functionality to determine which email addresses have registered accounts.

If a valid email is found, the system generates a secure, time-limited reset token (typically expiring after 1 hour) and sends it via email to the user's registered email address. Any previously generated reset tokens for the same user are invalidated.

If the email is not found, the system responds with the same generic message to maintain security, but no email is actually sent.

The user should check their email inbox for the reset link containing the token needed to complete the password reset process.

token.description:
Password reset token received via email.

This token is a cryptographically random, single-use token generated during the password reset request flow. It serves as proof of authorization for changing the password without requiring the current password.

The token must be valid, not expired (typically expires after 1 hour), and not previously used. The system validates these conditions before allowing the password change. Tokens are at least 32 characters long to prevent guessing attacks.

This token is sent to the user's registered email address in the initial password reset request and must be provided to complete the password reset process.

new_password.description:
New password for the user account.

The password must meet security requirements: minimum 8 characters, containing at least one letter and one number. The system validates password strength before accepting it.

This is the plain text password provided by the user, which will be hashed using industry-standard algorithms (bcrypt, argon2, or PBKDF2) before being stored in the password_hash field of the todo_list_users table.

The new password replaces the existing password_hash and should be different from the previous password, though the system cannot enforce this without storing password history.

ITodoListUser.IPasswordResetVerification.description:
Request body for verifying password reset token and setting new password.

This DTO is used in the second step of the password reset workflow, after the user has requested a password reset and received the reset token via email. It contains the reset token for validation and the new password the user wants to set.

The password reset verification process validates multiple security requirements. First, it checks that the reset token is valid and matches a pending reset request in the system. Second, it verifies the token has not expired (tokens typically have a 1-hour validity window). Third, it ensures the token has not been previously used, as reset tokens are single-use only for security.

The new password must meet all security requirements defined in the business rules: minimum length of 8 characters, containing at least one letter and one number. Some systems may also encourage special characters, though this is not mandatory for the minimal version. The password strength is validated before the system accepts the change.

Upon successful password reset, the system performs several security actions. The new password is hashed using industry-standard algorithms and stored in the password_hash field of the todo_list_users table, replacing the old hash. All existing user sessions (todo_list_user_sessions records) are invalidated, forcing the user to log in again on all devices. This ensures that if the account was compromised, the attacker's access is immediately revoked. A confirmation email is sent to the user's email address to notify them of the password change.

This operation does not require authentication since it is part of the account recovery process for users who have forgotten their password. However, possession of the valid reset token serves as proof of authorization to change the password.

Security considerations include validating token format and authenticity, checking token expiration, ensuring single-use token consumption, validating new password strength, preventing timing attacks during token validation, and maintaining audit trails of password reset attempts.

message.description:
Confirmation message indicating successful password reset.

This message informs the user that their password has been successfully changed and provides guidance on next steps, such as logging in with the new password.

The message provides clear feedback to complete the password reset user journey and confirms the security action was completed successfully.

email.description:
Email address of the user account for which the password was reset.

This confirms which account was affected by the password reset operation, providing transparency and helping users verify the correct account was modified.

The email address corresponds to the email field in the todo_list_users table and matches the account associated with the reset token that was validated.

ITodoListUser.IPasswordResetConfirmation.description:
Confirmation response returned after successful password reset verification and update.

This response type confirms to the user that their password reset request has been completed successfully. It is returned by the password reset verification endpoint after validating the reset token and updating the user's password_hash in the todo_list_users table.

The confirmation includes a success message and the email address of the affected account. This provides clear feedback to the user that the password change was successful and confirms which account was modified, which is important for security transparency.

After receiving this confirmation, users should proceed to log in with their new password. All existing sessions (todo_list_user_sessions) have been invalidated as a security measure, requiring fresh authentication on all devices.

current_password.description:
The user's current password for verification purposes.

This field is required to ensure that the password change request is legitimate and that an attacker who has gained access to an authenticated session cannot change the password without knowing the original password. The system validates this password against the stored password_hash in the todo_list_users table using secure comparison methods that prevent timing attacks.

The current password must match the user's existing password exactly. If it does not match, the password change operation will fail with an authentication error.

new_password.description:
The new password that the user wants to set for their account.

This password must meet all security requirements defined in the business rules: minimum 8 characters in length, containing at least one letter, and containing at least one number. The system will validate the new password against these requirements before accepting it.

If the new password fails validation, the operation will return a detailed error message specifying which requirements were not met. The password will be securely hashed using industry-standard algorithms (bcrypt, argon2, or PBKDF2) before being stored in the password_hash field of the todo_list_users table.

ITodoListUser.IChangePassword.description:
Request body for changing the authenticated user's password.

This schema represents the data required to securely change a user's password. The password change process requires both the current password for verification and the new password that will replace it. This two-password approach ensures that even if an attacker gains access to an authenticated session, they cannot change the password without knowing the original password.

The current_password field serves as an additional security verification step. The system will validate this password against the stored password_hash in the todo_list_users table before proceeding with the password change. This prevents session hijacking attacks from completely taking over an account.

The new_password field must meet all password strength requirements: minimum 8 characters, at least one letter, and at least one number. The system validates the new password before accepting it and provides detailed error messages if validation fails.

success.description:
Indicates whether the logout operation completed successfully.

This boolean value confirms that the administrator's current session has been properly terminated and the access token has been invalidated. A true value means the admin has been logged out from their current device/browser session and must re-authenticate to access the system again.

The success flag provides immediate feedback to the client application, allowing it to clear local authentication state, redirect to the login page, and update the UI appropriately.

message.description:
Human-readable confirmation message about the logout operation.

This message provides clear feedback to the administrator that their session has been successfully terminated. It serves both as a confirmation of the action and as user-facing communication that can be displayed in the admin interface.

Typical messages include confirmation that the session has ended and guidance about needing to log in again for future access. The message maintains a professional tone appropriate for administrative interfaces.

ITodoListAdminAuth.ILogoutResponse.description:
Response object returned after successfully logging out the current administrator session.

This response confirms that the admin's active session has been terminated by setting the expired_at timestamp in the todo_list_admin_sessions table. The logout operation invalidates the current JWT access token, requiring the administrator to authenticate again to regain access to the system.

The response provides both a boolean success indicator and a human-readable message to inform the admin that their session has ended. After receiving this response, client applications should clear stored authentication tokens, reset authentication state, and redirect the admin to the login page.

This operation affects only the current session from which the logout request was made, allowing the administrator to remain logged in on other devices if they have multiple active sessions. The session termination is recorded with a timestamp for security auditing and compliance purposes.

success.description:
Indicates whether the global logout operation completed successfully.

This boolean value confirms that all of the administrator's active sessions across all devices and browsers have been properly terminated. A true value means every session has been expired and all existing JWT access tokens for this admin are now invalid, requiring re-authentication on every device.

The success flag provides immediate feedback about the completion of this critical security operation, allowing the client application to update its authentication state and inform the administrator that access has been revoked everywhere.

message.description:
Human-readable confirmation message about the global logout operation.

This message provides clear feedback to the administrator that all their sessions have been successfully terminated across all devices. It communicates the scope of the operation and confirms that re-authentication will be required on every device where they were previously logged in.

Typical messages include confirmation of the global logout and explanation that the admin must log in again on all devices. The message maintains a professional tone appropriate for security-critical operations in administrative interfaces.

sessions_terminated.description:
The total number of active sessions that were terminated by this operation.

This count represents how many distinct admin sessions were expired, providing visibility into the scope of the logout action. Each session corresponds to a separate login from a specific device or browser, so this number indicates how many locations the admin was actively logged in from.

For example, if an admin was logged in from their laptop, phone, and tablet, this value would be 3. This information is valuable for security monitoring - an unexpectedly high number might indicate unauthorized access, while a count of 1 suggests the admin was only logged in from the current device.

The count includes the current session from which the logout request was made, so the minimum value for a successful operation is 1.

ITodoListAdminAuth.ILogoutAllResponse.description:
Response object returned after successfully logging out the administrator from all active sessions across all devices.

This response confirms that a global logout operation has been executed, terminating every active session for the authenticated administrator by setting the expired_at timestamp for all session records in the todo_list_admin_sessions table where expired_at was previously null. This comprehensive session termination invalidates all existing JWT access tokens for this admin, requiring re-authentication on every device and browser where they were logged in.

The response provides a success indicator, a human-readable confirmation message, and critically, a count of how many sessions were terminated. This session count gives the administrator visibility into how many active logins existed and were revoked, which is valuable for security awareness and monitoring.

This global logout functionality is essential for security scenarios such as suspected account compromise, lost devices, forgotten logouts on public computers, or deliberate security policy enforcement. After receiving this response, the admin must log in again on every device to regain access to the system. The operation creates a complete audit trail with expiration timestamps for all affected sessions, supporting security monitoring and compliance requirements.

email.description:
Updated email address for the administrator account.

When provided, this replaces the current email address associated with the admin account. The new email must follow valid email format and must be unique across all admin accounts in the system. If the email is already in use by another admin, the update will be rejected to maintain uniqueness constraints.

Changing the email address updates the login credentials for the administrator. After a successful email change, the admin should use the new email address for future authentication attempts. The system validates the email format before accepting the update to ensure data integrity.

password.description:
New password for the administrator account.

When provided, this updates the admin's authentication password. The password must meet security requirements: minimum 8 characters in length, containing at least one letter and at least one number. The system encourages the use of special characters for additional security, though they are not mandatory in the minimal version.

The provided password is in plain text format in the request body, but the system securely hashes it using industry-standard algorithms (bcrypt, argon2, or PBKDF2) before storage. The password is never stored in plain text. After a successful password change, all existing admin sessions may be invalidated for security purposes, requiring the admin to log in again with the new credentials.

This field is optional - if omitted, the current password remains unchanged. Only provide this field when the admin explicitly wants to change their password.

ITodoListAdmin.IUpdate.description:
Update request for administrator profile information.

Contains the fields that can be modified when an authenticated administrator updates their own profile. Both email and password updates are optional - the admin can choose to update either field, both fields, or submit an update with neither field changed (though the latter would be a no-op).

Email updates must maintain uniqueness across all admin accounts. If the provided email is already associated with another admin account, the update will fail with a validation error. The system performs email format validation to ensure the provided email follows standard email address patterns.

Password updates enforce security requirements to ensure strong authentication credentials. The minimum requirements are 8 characters with at least one letter and one number. The password is provided in plain text in the request (transmitted over HTTPS in production), but is immediately hashed using secure algorithms before storage. The system never logs or stores passwords in recoverable form.

When any field is successfully updated, the updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current time by the system. This provides an audit trail of when the account was last modified. The operation returns the complete updated admin profile (excluding the password hash) upon successful modification.

id.description:
